title: Geometry of the maximal-ideal blowup of a regular local surface
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a regular local ring of Krull dimension $2$, where $k=A/\mathfrak m$, and let $b:Y=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathfrak m}(\operatorname{Spec}A)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be the blowup of its reduced closed point. Then $Y$ is Noetherian and regular. The scheme-theoretic fibre $E=b^{-1}(\mathfrak m)$ is an effective Cartier divisor isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1_k$. For every closed point $q$ of $E$, the local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,q}$ is regular local of dimension $2$. Here the ideal of an effective Cartier divisor is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor. Conventions: [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [pqf-def-locnoeth], [def-nagata-global-blowup], [def-weil-residue-field], [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal].

The closed-point dimension assertion is the local calculation in the proof of 0AGR: a local equation for E is a nonzerodivisor and the quotient is the one-dimensional regular local ring of a closed point of the projective line; the regular-mod-x argument there gives dimension 2. Noetherianity follows from the finite-type blowup of Spec A.

proof.text: By regular localness choose $x,y\in\mathfrak m$ generating $\mathfrak m$, and apply the regular-parameter theorem to obtain regular sequences in both orders. The two-parameter atlas theorem applies to $I=\mathfrak m$ (regular localness includes Noetherianity). It gives a Noetherian scheme $Y$, its two charts $C_x=A[t]/(xt-y)$ and $C_y=A[u]/(yu-x)$, and the fibre's nonzerodivisor equations $x,y$. Thus the actual scheme-theoretic fibre $E$ is an effective Cartier divisor.

proof.text: Since $A/\mathfrak m=k$ is a field, apply the exceptional-fibre gluing theorem to the same $x,y$. It identifies the fibre charts with $k[t]$ and $k[u]$, their overlap with $k[t,t^{-1}]$ and transition $u=t^{-1}$. The specified chart maps glue to a $k$-isomorphism $E\cong\mathbf P^1_k$; all its local rings are regular local.

proof.text: For any point $q\in Y$, choose an atlas chart containing it and its pair $(g,h)=(x,y)$ or $(y,x)$, so the chart ring is $C=A[z]/(gz-h)$ with $z=h/g$. The affine-open stalk theorem identifies $\mathcal O_{Y,q}$ with $C_{\mathfrak p}$ for the corresponding prime $\mathfrak p$. As $(g,h)$ generates $\mathfrak m$ and $\dim A=2$, it is a regular system of parameters, and the parameter-blowup algebra theorem with $d=2$, $J=\{1,2\}$, $t_j=g$, $t_i=h$, $u_i=z$ applies to exactly this ring: $C_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular local whether or not $g\in\mathfrak p$. Since $Y$ is locally Noetherian by step 1, the local-ring characterization of regular schemes proves that $Y$ is regular.

Chart regularity, exceptional quotient and complement as in Illusie--Laszlo--Orgogozo, Travaux de Gabber, Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9 (printed p. 121), carried by lem-trf-parameter-blowup-algebra-regular; old item proof steps 6--9.

proof.text: Let $q$ be closed in $E$ and take $C,\mathfrak p$ as in step 3; $g\in\mathfrak p$ because $E$ is cut out by $g$ on the chart (step 1). The parameter-blowup algebra theorem gives $C/(g)\cong(A/\mathfrak m)[z]=k[z]$, $C$ Noetherian and $g$ injective on $C$. Hence $R=\mathcal O_{Y,q}=C_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian local by the localization theorem, $g/1$ lies in its maximal ideal and is a nonzerodivisor (if $(g/1)(a/s)=0$ then $vga=0$ for some $v\notin\mathfrak p$, so $va=0$ and $a/s=0$), and $R/gR\cong k[z]_{\overline{\mathfrak p}}$, $\overline{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak p/(g)$. As $\{q\}$ is closed in $E\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}k[z]$, $\overline{\mathfrak p}$ is maximal; the maximal-localization dimension theorem with $n=1$ gives $\dim R/gR=1$, and the nonzerodivisor quotient formula gives $\dim R=2$. With step 3 this is regular localness and dimension two at every closed point of $E$, including non-$k$-rational ones.
